title: Following a larger swimmer
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: The fish benefits and the shark is assumed unaffected, making this stipulated case commensalism. Effects can differ in other situations.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: A pilot fish gains food scraps near a shark; assume the shark has no appreciable benefit or harm in this example. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Pilot fish and Shark, in that order? Pilot fish: +; Shark: 0. The fish benefits and the shark is assumed unaffected, making this stipulated case commensalism. Effects can differ in other situations.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.

Recall: What term describes the Pilot fish–Shark interaction as stated in the lesson? The fish benefits and the shark is assumed unaffected, making this stipulated case commensalism. Effects can differ in other situations.
